analysis.title: September CPI Recap: Hotter print --> Live October Meeting
key_insights: September CPI was hotter than anticipated and broad-based, which Natixis says will stoke concerns that the summer lull in price pressures was a blip.
Headline CPI rose 0.6% m/m (0.4% in August) and core CPI rose 0.34% m/m (0.29% in August). Gasoline rose 9.1% m/m (prev. 3.9%) and accounted for over half of the monthly all-items increase.
Recreation and education and communication commodities were hot, pushing core goods prices up 0.25% m/m. Higher rents and hotels pushed shelter prices up 0.37% m/m.
Supercore CPI was softer than in August, at 0.42% m/m.
On the year, headline CPI rose 3.7% (from 3.4%) and core CPI rose 2.6% (from 2.4%). Core CPI rose 3.41% on a 3-month annualized basis and 2.85% on a 6-month annualized basis.

After August's disappointing print, Natixis had been optimistic on the inflation trajectory, but says that confidence takes a hit from the broad pressures in September. It had said a print near consensus would not shift the Fed narrative for October, but this one is far enough from consensus to make it a debate.

Natixis expects the Fed to pause at its October meeting. It calls avoiding a hike prudent because it leaves time to assess the data before the December meeting and avoids the political fallout of hiking just before the early-November mid-term elections.
The data gives the hawks more ammunition. If markets keep pricing a hike, the FOMC may be loath to surprise with a hold.
